question.text: How many shrimp per year will be covered by SWP's Humane Slaughter Initiative agreements on July 1, 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the Shrimp Welfare Project's estimated "[Shrimpact](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)" (in billions of shrimp helped in expectation per year) when checked by Metaculus on or soon after July 1, 2027.
question.fine_print:
The question will resolve as the headline estimated Shrimpact, regardless of any estimated range. If SWP ceases to provide a headline estimate and instead provides only a range, however, the question will resolve as the midpoint of the range.

The total Shrimpact will be rounded, if necessary, to the nearest 100 million shrimp.

research:
I checked the live Shrimpact page and SWP's blog. The headline figure is now about 6.5 billion, up from the 6.3 billion the question cites for September 2026. Nothing yet settles the question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-04 (fetched): the [Shrimpact page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact) gives a headline of **about 6.5 billion shrimps helped per year (in expectation)**, with a range of **4.5 to 9 billion**. It also gives about 1,400 shrimps per $ per year.
  - The page does not date the headline figure. It refers to an "October 2026 Shrimpact graphic", so the figure probably dates from October 2026, but that is my inference.
- Basis: 37 corporate agreements in 9 countries, totalling 89,774 metric tonnes per year once all stunners are working. The page calls the figure "a projection based on signed commitments - not a count of shrimp that have already been stunned." [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- By country: Vietnam 2.54B, Honduras 1.3B, India 630M, Indonesia 570M, Ecuador 480M, Sri Lanka 440M, Venezuela 280M, Thailand 180M, Nigeria 72M. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- Installed so far: 20 stunners commissioned, covering 54,175 MT, or about 3.6B shrimp per year. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- Retailer commitments (Tesco, M&S, ALDI Nord/Süd) are not counted in the headline. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. At 6.5B, the current value is **below the question's lower bound of 6.95B**. It needs to rise by at least about 0.45B by July 2027 to land inside the range.
- The FAQ now separates "committed impact", "installed capacity" and "verified use", and says verified-use monitoring is "still being strengthened." If SWP ever switched the headline to installed or verified figures, it would fall sharply, to about 3.6B or less. I found no sign that such a change is planned. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10/11: the agreement count is now 37. Charity Entrepreneurship separately reports ">6 billion" shrimp from 36 stunner agreements. [CE](https://www.charityentrepreneurship.com/shrimp-welfare-project), [HSI page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/humane-slaughter-initiative)
- 2026-10-16: an ICAW report on shrimp welfare and French retailer commitments was published, according to the collected news. It has no direct effect on the Shrimpact figure. [source](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-09: the question background puts Shrimpact at 6.3B.
- 2026-08: ACE's review estimated about 6.1B per year from about 33 MOUs signed by H1 2026. It flagged uncertainty about whether stunners are used correctly. [Wikipedia summary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp_Welfare_Project)
- 2026-06-29: a trade article on stunners in Southeast Asia says Honduran producer Seajoy was waiting for its third stunner. [source](https://aquaasiapac.com/2026/06/29/improving-shrimp-welfare-with-electrical-stunners-in-southeast-asia/)
- 2026-01-14: Trang Corporation (Vietnam) and Dary Foods joined, committing 1,800 MT per year. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/trangs-group-trang-corporation-dary-foods-join-humane-slaughter-partnership-with-shrimp-welfare-project)
- 2025-12-01: C.P. Viet Nam and Westbridge joined. C.P. Viet Nam will stun 100% of the L. vannamei it harvests for the UK from 2026-01-01. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/cpvietnam-westbridge-food-group-join-shrimp-welfare-project-electrical-stunning-programme)
- I found no SWP blog post announcing a new partner after January 2026. The blog seems to lag behind the agreement count.

## 4. Base rates / trend
- Earlier snapshot, date unknown (probably early to mid 2025): about 2.6B, range 1.8 to 3.6B, at 1,600 shrimps per $. [source](https://shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact)
- 2025-09-16: about 4.0B with 21 MOUs. [source](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/major-milestone-for-humane-slaughter-shrimp-welfare-project-expected-to-help-4-billion-shrimps-annually-new-mou-with-camimex-seafood-connection)
- 2025-12: about 4.5B with 26 MOUs, from SWP's EA Forum post, as reported in a search summary. I could not open the post because of a 429 error. [source](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimps)
- 2026 H1: about 6.1B with about 33 MOUs (ACE).
- 2026-09: 6.3B. 2026-10/11: 6.5B with 37 agreements.
- Trend:
  - Sep 2025 to Oct/Nov 2026 rose about 2.5B in about 13 to 14 months, roughly 0.18B per month.
  - Dec 2025 to mid 2026 rose about 1.6B in about 7 months.
  - Sep to Oct/Nov 2026 rose only 0.2B, so growth has slowed recently.
  - Each new agreement adds about 0.05 to 0.4B. The 1,900 to 2,000 MT minimum is about 0.13B. Since Sep 2025, each extra agreement has added about 0.15B on average.
- The roughly 8 months from now to July 2027 cover a similar span to past windows that saw gains of +0.5B (Sep to Dec 2025) and +1.6B (Dec 2025 to mid 2026). The headline figure has never fallen in the snapshots I found.
- SWP's stated long-term goal is "100 billion per year by 2030" through regional adoption. [source](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimps)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on SWP Shrimpact. None of the markets in the collected price list relate to this question.
- I could not find the Metaculus community forecast for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- New MOU signings. Large Vietnamese, Ecuadorian or Indian producers could add 0.3B or more each. A SeafoodSource article mentions the 30th MOU, but I could not open it because of a 403 error. [source](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/aquaculture/uk-nonprofit-ensuring-viability-of-shrimp-welfare-commitments-through-electrical-stunner-agreements)
- Possible methodology changes, such as tonnage-to-count conversions or a shift toward verified-use reporting. Either could move the headline down.
- SWP's year-end and fundraising updates (Dec 2026, Giving Season) and the EA Forum or ACE cycles in 2026-27 often bring announcements or refreshed figures.
- Pressure from retailer commitments (UK/EU, the French ICAW report) could push more producers into agreements. Retailer commitments themselves are not counted in the headline.

## SWP Shrimpact forecast research (Humane Slaughter Initiative), as of 2026-11-04

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-04 (fetched today): The [Shrimpact page](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/shrimpact) gives a headline of **about 6.5 billion shrimp per year in expectation**, with a range of 4.5 to 9 billion. It also says about 1,400 shrimp are helped per dollar per year (range 970 to 1,900).
  - The headline number has no date on it. The page refers to an October 2026 image and an August 2026 article.
  - The figure comes from 37 agreements with producers in 9 countries. Once all stunners are working, they are expected to cover about 89,774 tonnes of shrimp per year.
  - 20 of the 37 stunners are installed and commissioned, covering about 54,175 tonnes, or roughly 3.6 billion shrimp per year.
  - Retailer policies (Tesco, M&S, ALDI and others) are listed separately and are not counted in the Shrimpact figure.
- Breakdown by country, from the same page: Vietnam ~2.54B, Honduras ~1.3B, India ~630M, Indonesia ~570M, Ecuador ~480M, Sri Lanka ~440M, Venezuela ~280M, Thailand ~180M, Nigeria ~72M.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The current value (6.5B) is below the bottom of the question's range (6.95B).
- The figure would need to rise by about 0.45B or more by July 1, 2027 to land inside the range.
- I could not get to the Wayback Machine, so I could not confirm exactly when the figure moved from 6.3B (the question's September 2026 number) to 6.5B.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-16: The ICAW report on shrimp farming in France cites 440B farmed shrimp a year. It does not report any new SWP agreement. [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-09 (per the question background): Shrimpact stood at 6.3B.
- 2026-08-24: SWP announced a three-way validation deal between Confremarca (Ecuador), Klaas Puul and Albert Heijn, with stunner use tracked in a database SWP runs. [Shrimp Insights](https://www.shrimpinsights.com/advertorial/future-shrimp-welfare-how-retailers-can-validate-electrical-stunning-commitments)
- 2026-08: According to Wikipedia, Animal Charity Evaluators' (ACE) review said the agreements could cover about 6.1B shrimp a year once everything is operational. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp_Welfare_Project)
- Undated, probably 2026: SeafoodSource reported that SWP signed its 30th agreement with a producer. Producers must commit to about 2,000 tonnes a year and get a major buyer to co-sign. I could not open the article to confirm the date. [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/aquaculture/uk-nonprofit-ensuring-viability-of-shrimp-welfare-commitments-through-electrical-stunner-agreements)
- 2026-06-01: This is the latest post I found on SWP's blog. The blog does not seem to announce every new agreement: the page counts 37, but the last agreement announcement I found was the 25th, in January 2026. [SWP blog](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog)
- 2026-01-14: Trang Corporation and Dary Foods signed the 25th agreement (the 9th in Vietnam), committing to 1,800 tonnes a year. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/trangs-group-trang-corporation-dary-foods-join-humane-slaughter-partnership-with-shrimp-welfare-project)

### 4. Base rates and trend
These are the headline figures I could find over time:
- 2025-05-15: 3.3B per year from 17 agreements; under 40% of those stunners had been deployed as of April 2025. [EA Forum comment](https://ea.greaterwrong.com/posts/2wnQCmyPRwdL9hWsD/how-to-help-neglected-animals/comment/ihgzr4y3dQwa22yZ2)
- 2025-09-16: About 4B per year at the 21st agreement (CAMIMEX). [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/major-milestone-for-humane-slaughter-shrimp-welfare-project-expected-to-help-4-billion-shrimps-annually-new-mou-with-camimex-seafood-connection)
- Late 2025: About 4.5B per year from 24 agreements. This comes from SWP's EA Forum posts, whose exact date I could not confirm. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimps)
- 2026-08: 6.1B (ACE, via Wikipedia).
- 2026-09: 6.3B (question background).
- 2026-11-04: 6.5B from 37 agreements.

What the trend implies:
- The figure has gone up about +3.2B in roughly 18 months, which is about 0.18B a month. From August to November 2026 it rose about 0.13B a month.
- Each new agreement adds roughly 0.1 to 0.3B. The smallest country total is Nigeria at about 72M; most producers commit around 1,800 to 2,000 tonnes, which works out to roughly 120M or more shrimp.
- If the recent pace holds for 8 more months, the figure would add about 1.0 to 1.5B, but that is just a projection from past growth.
- Every value I found went up, and I found no downward revisions. Still, the figure depends on SWP's methodology, so it could be revised either way, for example if a partner drops out or the tonnage-to-shrimp conversion changes.
- The page updates without a regular schedule.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction market prices supplied (Kalshi, Polymarket) relate to this question.
- I found nothing on Manifold or from expert forecasters about Shrimpact. I did not check the Metaculus community forecast for this question.
- SWP's own goal is "100 billion+ per year as soon as 2030". That is an aspiration, not a forecast. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/PHgbyFu4ikJRKPqx9/shrimp-welfare-project-s-path-to-helping-100-billion-shrimps)

### 6. Upcoming events that could move the number
- New producer agreements, particularly large Vietnamese, Indian, Ecuadorian or Indonesian exporters co-signed with UK or EU buyers. Retailer deadlines create demand here, for example Tesco's commitment to 100% electrically stunned farmed shrimp by 2026.
- ACE's 2026 charity recommendations, likely in November 2026 (the 2025 ones came out on 2025-11-04). These could affect SWP's funding and therefore its budget for stunners.
- Year-end or annual impact updates and possible changes to SWP's methodology. Its 2030 plan of shifting stunner costs onto industry could change how many stunners SWP funds itself.
- Stunner commissioning (currently 20 of 37) does not change the headline, which already counts all signed agreements.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 8 months. Forecasts close on 2027-06-01 and the question resolves on or soon after 2027-07-01.

(b) **Latest known value:** About 6.5 billion shrimp per year in expectation, with a range of 4.5 to 9 billion. This is from the Shrimpact page fetched on 2026-11-04 and probably dates from October 2026. It is based on 37 agreements covering 89,774 MT.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 6.5 billion, i.e. 6,500,000,000.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- The trend since September 2025 is about 0.18 billion per month, which would give roughly 7.9 to 8.0 billion.
- The more recent pace of about 0.1 billion per month would give about 7.3 billion.
- A central estimate is around 7.5 to 7.7 billion.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over comparable windows of about 8 months, the figure has risen by between 0.5 billion (Sep to Dec 2025) and 1.6 billion (Dec 2025 to mid 2026). It has never fallen in the snapshots found. Updates are lumpy: one large Vietnamese, Ecuadorian or Indian producer can add 0.3 to 1 billion at once, and the page may go months without an update.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** No market exists. SWP's own goal of 100 billion by 2030 is aspirational and implies much faster regional adoption than the trend. The question creator's range of 7 to 12 billion leans slightly higher than the trend.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** SWP switches the headline to installed or verified capacity (about 3.6 billion or less), or revises its tonnage-to-count conversion downward, or partners drop out. Alternatively, the page simply goes unrefreshed and stays at 6.5 billion.
- **High:** A major integrator or a regional industry association signs on, for example a Vietnamese association deal or a large Ecuadorian exporter, adding several billion. Retailer-driven supplier mandates could also cascade into many MOUs.
